abstract_en: Passive daytime radiative cooling materials (RCs) maintain low surface temperatures under sunlight and can reduce building cooling loads and urban overheating. However, RCs with static optical properties overcool in cold seasons, and adaptive RCs proposed to date rely on temperature/humidity to switch their optical/radiative properties. Further, they address either daytime or nighttime response and are subject to ageing and to false switching on mild sunlit winter days. Here, we propose a system to seasonally modulate RCs with angular solar absorption, achieved with L-shaped fins, and with thermal energy storage (TES), implemented with phase change materials (PCMs) and concrete mass. The L-shaped fins have solar-absorptive, equator-facing walls shaded by horizontal eaves, enabling high direct solar absorption only at the low solar elevations of winter, with RC film on all other surfaces. Coupled with TES, the system is an angular-dependent thermal-mass-enhanced radiative cooler (ATMRC). In field campaigns in Western Sydney, the finned RC samples reached winter daytime surface temperatures 6–9 °C above the static RC and up to 11 °C above the unfinned RC + TES, resolving the daytime overcooling that TES alone introduces. The ATMRC with the 8 °C PCM reduced winter dew and frost durations by 56% and 73%, respectively, relative to the static RC. The summer daytime penalty against the static RC was 2 °C. abstract_en: Radiative cooling roofs can reduce cooling demand and achieve subambient surface temperatures under sunlight, but their high solar reflectance can increase heating demand during cold periods. Switchable albedo radiative cooling roofs may mitigate this seasonal trade-off by switching between cooling and heating states. However, their annual building energy effects across different climates remain insufficiently quantified. This study evaluated a mechanically switchable albedo radiative cooling roof using a U.S. Department of Energy strip mall prototype in eight U.S. cities representing distinct climate zones. Four roof configurations were compared: a baseline roof, a traditional cool roof, a non-switchable radiative cooling roof, and a switchable albedo radiative cooling roof. A retrospective monthly state selection procedure was used to combine the results of two fixed-state annual simulations. The modeled coating, based on properties reported in the literature, changed from a solar reflectance of 0.93 under mechanical stretching to 0.05 under mechanical compression while maintaining high thermal emissivity. In climates dominated by cooling demand, the switchable albedo radiative cooling roofs and non-switchable radiative cooling roofs produced similar cooling benefits. In moderate and cold climates, switching avoided annual heating energy penalties while reducing annual cooling electricity use by 12.0–22.8% relative to the baseline. title_en: Construction of Uniform Thermal Network in Passive Radiative Cooling Coatings by Nanocellulose-Mediated Pickering Emulsion Template
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Developing high-performance passive radiative cooling coatings (PRCC) with high thermal conductivity for fast heat dissipation from self-heating objects remains a significant challenge. In this study, a nanocellulose-mediated Pickering emulsion strategy was employed to construct a uniform hexagonal boron nitride (BN) thermal network within PRCC. Benefiting from the Pickering emulsion template stabilized by TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibrils (TOCNF), BN nanosheets and other functional inorganic nanoparticles were uniformly dispersed in the PRCC matrix, forming a continuous and homogeneous thermally conductive network. This structural design endowed the PRCC with excellent thermal conductivity, high solar reflectance in the solar spectrum (0.3–2.5 μm), and strong emissivity in the “atmospheric window” (ATSW, 8–13 μm). Specifically, the thermal conductivity of the TOCNF-BN-modified PRCC reached 2.28 ± 0.15 W·m−1·K−1, which was significantly higher than that of the pristine PRCC. The coating exhibited a solar reflectivity of ~87% and an emissivity of ~93% in the ATSW. Outdoor model temperature tests indicated that the internal temperature of the PRCC-TOCNF-BN-coated metal cabinet was 9.6 °C lower than that of the bare cabinet and 6.7 °C lower than the cabinet coated with pristine PRCC. This novel approach of using Pickering emulsion templates to fabricate highly thermally conductive radiative cooling coatings provides a new strategy for the development of high-performance and multifunctional radiative cooling materials for thermal management applications.

title_zh: Robust Radiative Cooling in Functionalizable Silica Microsphere Paints
title_en: Robust Radiative Cooling in Functionalizable Silica Microsphere Paints
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Abstract Disordered coatings based on silica microspheres provide a scalable and robust platform for passive daytime radiative cooling. While particle-size optimization is often considered critical for enhancing solar scattering, the role of microsphere diameter once a coating operates in the multiple-scattering regime remains unclear. Here, we characterize the radiative cooling performance of disordered, multiply scattering photonic glass coatings with diameters ranging from 2 to 8 μm, deposited on a highly reflective substrate. Despite measurable differences in microscopic scattering properties, both the spectral radiative response and the net cooling performance are robust to variations in particle diameter within the investigated range. Outdoor thermal measurements reveal nearly identical steady-state temperature reductions across the full size range. These results identify this robustness as a property of the complete coating–substrate architecture: in the solar range, multiple scattering and the reflective substrate act together to maintain high reflectance, while in the mid-infrared range, the response is dominated by the intrinsic Si–O absorption of the silica layer. This robustness enables microsphere size to be selected based on surface chemistry or processing constraints without compromising cooling performance.

title_zh: Biobased Boston Ivy‐Inspired Cryogel Integrating Radiative Cooling and Phase Change Energy Storage for Adaptive Thermal Regulation
title_en: Biobased Boston Ivy‐Inspired Cryogel Integrating Radiative Cooling and Phase Change Energy Storage for Adaptive Thermal Regulation
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Boston ivy is a traditional plant for building heat management through shading and transpiration. Inspired by its “vine‐leaf” system, we design a bionic cryogel that functionalizes daytime cooling and nighttime thermal buffering, promoting sustainable and comfortable housing and living environments. The aligned channels mimic vine tendrils, delivering an ultralow radial thermal conductivity (0.035 W m −1 ·K −1 ), high solar reflectance (95.28%), and high infrared emissivity (97.04%). Embedded phase‐change materials (PCMs) present leaf‐like, functionalized structures that store excess solar energy during the daytime and release latent heat at night, achieving 6.2°C sub‐ambient cooling under sunlight. In darkness, the stored latent heat is released, keeping the cryogel 2.4°C above ambient and preventing nocturnal overcooling. This spatiotemporal synergy between daytime radiative cooling and nighttime heat release enables climate‐adaptive thermal management, reducing the urban heat buildup with no need for electricity consumption. Our bionic design shifts thermal regulation from passive adaptation to active thermal planning using low carbon footprint materials as proven by life cycle assessment (LCA), offering a more sustainable pathway for energy‐efficient buildings.

title_zh: Radiative Cooling Floating Covers Cool Lakes and Suppress Evaporation
title_en: Radiative Cooling Floating Covers Cool Lakes and Suppress Evaporation
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Globally, warmer lakes disrupt thermal balance, causing hypoxia, salinization, biodiversity loss, and increased evaporation. Conventional floating covers used to reduce evaporation absorb sunlight and warm the underlying water, limiting suppression efficiency to less than the coverage ratio (η eff /Φ ≤ 1). Here, we break this limit by developing Superhydrophobic Radiative Cooling Covers (SRCC) via multi‐level structural design. SRCC actively cools the water surface by combining high solar reflectance, strong mid‐infrared emission, and superhydrophobicity. Experiments show SRCC lowers water temperature by 2.2°C versus uncovered water, achieving 93.1± 0.1% evaporation suppression at 91% coverage, yielding η eff /Φ > 1.0 for the first time. Large‑scale simulations for nine Chinese lakes indicate that SRCC reduces water temperature by 4.87°C (vs. no cover) and by 12.44 °C (vs. black covers). This cooling could increase annual freshwater reserves by 10.78 km 3 across China under full deployment, equivalent to 20.9 L per person per day. Unattainable with conventional covers, SRCC uniquely mitigates thermal accumulation while enhancing freshwater storage, providing a quantifiable engineering solution to climate‑driven water stress and enabling adaptive lake ecosystem management across regional and global scales.

abstract_en: Janus structures with directional thermal emission offer a promising route toward sub-ambient passive radiative cooling; however, the simultaneous realization of high visible transparency, strong mid-infrared emissivity, and mechanical robustness within a single platform remains a significant materials challenge. Here, we report a transparent Janus emitter (TJE) that integrates spectrally selective thermal radiation with excellent optical clarity and structural durability. The TJE is fabricated using a scalable microfabrication strategy involving microscale patterning of quartz, deposition of an ultrathin titanium film, and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) encapsulation, resulting in a dual-faced architecture with asymmetric thermal–radiative functionality. The emitter exhibits near-unity emissivity (0.97–0.98) within the 8–13 μm atmospheric window while maintaining high visible-light transmittance (∼90%). Both indoor and outdoor measurements demonstrate effective daytime radiative cooling, achieving near-ambient temperatures under strong solar irradiation. Mechanical and thermal reliability tests further confirm outstanding durability, with a flexural strength more than twice that of conventional glass and stable performance under repeated thermal cycling. title_zh: Hierarchical Nanofibrous Membranes With Fluorescent Competitive Absorption and Self‐Adaptive Thermal‐Wet Regulation for Radiative Cooling
title_en: Hierarchical Nanofibrous Membranes With Fluorescent Competitive Absorption and Self‐Adaptive Thermal‐Wet Regulation for Radiative Cooling
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) provides a zero‐energy thermal management strategy. Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) is suitable for electrospun cooling textiles due to its spinnability, flexibility, and high infrared emissivity, but it suffers from UV‐induced photothermal accumulation and aging. Here, we implement a nanoscale fluorescence‐competitive absorption strategy by incorporating fluorescent microspheres (FMs) whose excitation spectrum fully covers the UV absorption band of TPU. These FMs convert UV photons into visible emission, simultaneously reducing photothermal conversion, enhancing UV stability, and enabling coloration. A highly reflective, hierarchical nanofibrous underlayer with a hierarchical fiber‐diameter distribution, fabricated via high‐concentration electrospinning, further achieves broadband scattering, thereby yielding an overall effective solar reflectance (ESR sol ) of 96.7%. After 200 min of accelerated UV aging, the ESRsol decreases only slightly to 95.2%. The membrane exhibits a photoluminescence quantum yield of 63.3% and photon conversion efficiency of 53.2%. Meanwhile, integrated with a temperature‐responsive dynamic moisture management structure, it reaches an evaporative cooling power of 392.4 W·m −2 at 38°C and 262.9 W·m −2 at 25°C. A Monte Carlo simulation validates the nano‐ and microscale structural design, offering a promising approach toward adaptive personal thermal management textiles.

title_zh: A Switchable Dual‐Mode Janus Composite for All‐Weather Passive Radiative Cooling and Solar‐Joule Heating in Energy‐Efficient Buildings
title_en: A Switchable Dual‐Mode Janus Composite for All‐Weather Passive Radiative Cooling and Solar‐Joule Heating in Energy‐Efficient Buildings
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Adaptive thermal regulation across diurnal and seasonal cycles remains a critical challenge for energy‐efficient buildings. A switchable dual‐mode Janus‐structured composite is developed by integrating a polyoxymethylene fiber/acrylate resin/BaSO 4 aerogel cooling layer with a graphene aerogel/paraffin wax (PW) phase‐change composite heating layer to achieve synergistic passive radiative cooling, solar‐Joule heating, and latent‐heat storage. The heating layer exhibits high thermal conductivity, high solar‐to‐latent heat conversion efficiency, high latent heat capacity, and high electrical conductivity. This permits a maximum sub‐ambient temperature rise of 17.4°C across the day. The cooling layer delivers a solar reflectivity of 96.2%, a mid‐infrared emissivity of 94.0%, and a low thermal conductivity of 0.053 W m −1 K −1 , achieving a maximum sub‐ambient temperature drop of 21.3°C and a genuine radiative net cooling power of 110.4 W m −2 , with an additional transient thermal buffering provided by the latent heat of PW (239.7 J g −1 ). Outdoor tests verify diurnal regulation and paraffin‐induced temperature hysteresis. Building energy simulations across 15 Chinese cities demonstrate annual energy savings exceeding 10.8% in most regions, with reductions of 9.5 and 15.1 MJ m −2 in heating and cooling demands, respectively. This work provides an effective strategy for all‐weather thermal management and sustainable energy savings under diverse climatic conditions.

abstract_en: ABSTRACT Environmentally adaptive thermoregulation with visually appealing coloration is a critical requirement for smart textiles. Black/white color switching has been proposed to manipulate solar energy for fulfilling outdoor heating/cooling demands, but it optically conflicts with conventional coloration methods depending on chemical dyes to selectively absorb visible wavelengths. Here, we create a thermochromic structural color metafabric (TSCM) that undercores dynamic light manipulation across the visible, solar, and mid‐infrared bands, achieving unmet textile intelligence of temperature self‐regulation and multi‐chromatic display. TSCM consists of a poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) nanofiber substrate, a thermochromic microcapsule (TCM) layer, and an overlying photonic crystal coating. In low‐temperature environments, the photonic crystal selectively reflects bandgap‐visible wavelengths while the TCM absorbs most other visible light, enabling high‐saturation structural color and solar heating. At high temperatures, TCM transitions to a white, broadband reflective state, making the structural color fade; collaborating with the bottom‐layer mid‐infrared emissive nanofibers, the system achieves efficient radiative cooling. Under 1 kW m −2 solar irradiation, the metafabric maintains 35°C–40°C despite ambient variations from 15°C to 30°C, while exhibiting chromatic patterns. abstract_en: As the thermal backbone of urban energy infrastructure, transmission cables directly affect the stability and resilience of modern cities. However, high operating temperatures, driven by Joule heating and solar radiation, critically limit the ampacity of overhead transmission lines, particularly under extreme climate conditions. Such high temperatures constrain electricity delivery and pose systemic risks to essential services and long-term urban sustainability. To overcome this challenge, we adopt a high thermal conductivity radiative cooling (HTCRC) coating comprising hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanoparticles embedded in a polydimethylsiloxane matrix to reduce cable temperature. Enabled by photonic thermal management, this composite structure simultaneously achieves high solar reflectance (0.92) through efficient light scattering, strong mid-infrared emissivity via polymer vibrational modes (0.95), and enhanced thermal conductivity (1.28 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹). Outdoor experiments demonstrate notable daytime cooling of simulated HTCRC-coated power cables, maintaining safe operating temperatures even under intense solar exposure. In addition, thermal modeling based on the CIGRE 601 standard reveals a 6-10% increase in ampacity across representative hot-climate cities globally. title_zh: A broadband selective high-emissivity thin-film emitter for efficient passive radiative cooling
title_en: A broadband selective high-emissivity thin-film emitter for efficient passive radiative cooling
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Abstract Passive radiative cooling is a promising thermal management technology that requires no external energy to achieve cooling. By emitting thermal radiation through the atmospheric transparency window to the cold outer space, it can maintain a temperature below the ambient environment. In this work, a broadband selective-emissivity emitter for daytime radiative cooling is proposed. The presented emitter achieves strong solar reflectivity and enhanced thermal emissivity within the atmospheric window. Simulation findings demonstrate that the proposed thin-film structure possesses excellent reflective performance from 0.3 μ m to 2.5 μ m, achieving an average reflectivity of 0.98. Meanwhile, an average emissivity of 0.93 is obtained from 8 μ m to 13 μ m, enabling efficient thermal radiation to outer space. Owing to its broadband selective-emission characteristics, the emitter effectively enhances the spectral matching between thermal radiation and the atmospheric window. Based on thermal equilibrium equations, the net cooling heat flux of the emitter is determined to be 117.64 W m −2 under typical daytime conditions. Compared with conventional broadband emitters, the proposed structure concentrates thermal emission predominantly during the atmospheric window, exhibiting excellent broadband selective-emission characteristics. The proposed design also shows promising potential for energy-efficient buildings, electronic heat dissipation, and temperature regulation of photovoltaic systems.

title_zh: Hydration‐Induced Environmentally‐Adaptive Thermal Management with Microphase Separated Hydrogel
title_en: Hydration‐Induced Environmentally‐Adaptive Thermal Management with Microphase Separated Hydrogel
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT The heat stress associated with extreme weather has paved the way for the rapid development of passive cooling techniques, but they are unable to tolerate fluctuating thermal and hydric environments, and their cooling power is more than halved under harsh conditions. Reliable multimodal thermal management techniques to couple with dynamic weather conditions are highly sought‐after. Herein, we develop a phase‐separated hydrogel via water‐induced microphase separation of waterborne polyurethane with the assistance of a hygroscopic layered network for hierarchical structure engineering. The obtained hydrogel undergoes hydration‐induced structural evolution from a compact solid monolith to a layered porous architecture, delivering a solar modulation capacity of ∼0.8 together with a high mid‐infrared emissivity of ∼0.95. Such optical features enable the hydrogel to achieve dynamic thermal regulation with a 9°C temperature span and sub‐ambient radiative cooling (∼6°C) under direct solar radiation. Additionally, via in situ incorporation of a light absorber or hygroscopic agent, the hydrogel is endowed with dual‐mode solar heating/cooling functionality and synergistic dehumidification‐cooling performance, respectively. Furthermore, the manufacturing process for the as‐proposed hydrogel is green, sustainable, and scalable, which permits industrial‐size hydrogels with combinations of stability, durability, sustainability, and processability. This work provides a promising candidate to meet the need for integrated thermoregulatory systems for environment‐specific adaptation.

title_zh: Green Radiative Cooling and Antimicrobial Materials Based on Polylactic Acid Oligomer Hexagonal Microspheres
title_en: Green Radiative Cooling and Antimicrobial Materials Based on Polylactic Acid Oligomer Hexagonal Microspheres
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Thermal management by passive radiative cooling materials can save energy and reduce emission of green-house gas remarkably compared with traditional air-conditioner cooling. However, few of these materials are degradable, thus their disposal may lead to another environmental problem. Meanwhile, the COVID-19 pandemic and other infectious diseases have raised the requirement of hygienic and antimicrobial performance. This work reports a discovery that polylactic acid oligomer (PLAO) material possesses radiative cooling effect, wide-spectrum antimicrobial property and degradability, simultaneously. The radiative cooling effect is attribute to the hexagonal microsphere geometry and nanotexture of polylactic acid oligomer (PLAO) crystals, which enhance the reflectivity in the solar spectrum through multiple scattering effect and exhibit high emissivity in the mid-infrared atmospheric window. Hierarchically porous PLAO coating material realizes an apparent temperature reduction of 6.8 ℃ under irradiation of solar spectrum (AM 1.5). The material also shows wide-spectrum antimicrobial and anti-viral properties against coronaviruses (including COVID-19 virus), gram-positive bacteria, gram-negative bacteria, fungi and multidrug resistant bacteria.

title_zh: Bioinspired Homologous Gradient Interphase Sustains Phase‐Change Buffering and Radiative Cooling Under Thermal Shocks
title_en: Bioinspired Homologous Gradient Interphase Sustains Phase‐Change Buffering and Radiative Cooling Under Thermal Shocks
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Coupling phase‐change buffering with passive radiative cooling offers complementary continuous and transient regulation for personal thermal management (PTM). In fibrous systems, however, repeated phase transitions drive molecular rearrangement and thermomechanical stress accumulation, causing fiber deformation, pore collapse, and irreversible deterioration of radiative cooling performance. Herein, inspired by graded stress transfer in mussel byssus, we develop a homologous gradient interphase strategy to construct a core–gradient interphase–shell fibrous membrane (Ho‐GIFM) for durable PTM. During coaxial electrospinning, homologous polyethylene glycol‐based polyurethanes interdiffuse and entangle across the interface, while in situ UV crosslinking stabilizes the interphase. This structure redistributes phase‐change‐induced strain and constrains long‐range chain rearrangement, preserving phase‐change functionality and porous fiber networks. Ho‐GIFM exhibits a broad solid‐solid phase‐transition window (30.2–51.5°C) with a competitive melting enthalpy (60.2 J g −1 ). Notably, after 100 alternating thermal shocks between −40 and 80°C, Ho‐GIFM retains 99.0% of its initial solar reflectance versus only 74.5% for the heterogeneous counterpart, together with 99.9% mid‐infrared emissivity retention. Furthermore, it delivers a calculated daytime net radiative cooling power of 101.9 W m −2 and achieves an average synthetic‐skin temperature reduction of 14.9°C. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for durable PTM and multicomponent functional fibers.

title_zh: Optically clear mesoporous silica aerogels for passive daytime radiative cooling
title_en: Optically clear mesoporous silica aerogels for passive daytime radiative cooling
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: This study demonstrates the use of silica aerogel monoliths as optically transparent radiative cooling materials exhibiting near-unity emissivity in the 8–13 μm atmospheric transparency window. Silica is widely used for radiative cooling applications due to favorable optical properties. However, dense silica exhibits a reflectance peak around 9–9.5 μm due to the Reststrahlen effect, lowering emissivity near the blackbody peak (λ = 9.7 μm) at 300 K which substantially reduces cooling power. Previous approaches used complex photonic structures to enhance emissivity of silica-based radiative cooling materials. Here, a mesoporous microstructure of aerogels is demonstrated to eliminate this characteristic reflectance peak. The nanoparticles (∼4–5 nm radius) and pores (size distribution peak ∼9–20 nm) constituting the aerogel were much smaller than visible wavelengths, minimizing scattering and enabling >90% transmittance. Spectral emissivity and solar absorptance of these aerogels on metallic substrates were determined experimentally and numerically, showing high radiative cooling potential without needing complex nanostructures.

title_zh: Co-Assembled MOF@SiO2 Nanostructures for Superhydrophobic and Electrically Insulating Radiative Cooling Coatings
title_en: Co-Assembled MOF@SiO2 Nanostructures for Superhydrophobic and Electrically Insulating Radiative Cooling Coatings
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology, characterized by zero-energy cooling capability, has shown great promise for thermal management of high-voltage electrical equipment. However, such application scenarios impose stringent multifunctional requirements on PRC coatings, including superhydrophobicity to resist surface contamination, as well as high electrical insulation strength to prevent surface flashover. Here, we report a co-assembly strategy for constructing multifunctional PRC coatings through the in situ integration of a metal-organic framework (MOF) with a silica precursor. The appropriately tailored bandgap (Eg = 4.25 eV) of the MOF, slightly exceeding the upper photon-energy bound of the measured solar band (4.13 eV), enables suppressed solar absorption while affording a strong mid-infrared emissivity. Meanwhile, the high-Eg SiO2 shell effectively passivates intrinsic insulation defects and the high surface energy associated with MOFs, thereby enhancing both dielectric reliability and superhydrophobicity. Consequently, the optimized PRC coating delivered a temperature drop of 10.6 ± 0.5 °C during outdoor testing, together with robust superhydrophobicity (153.7°) and high wet flashover strength (15.6 kV/cm). This work advances PRC coatings beyond conventional thermal regulation by integrating radiative cooling, surface self-cleaning, and electrical insulation into a unified material platform, opening new opportunities for passive thermal management of high-voltage electrical equipment.

abstract_en: Conspectus Spectral modulation, the precise control over light reflection, transmission, absorption, and scattering, has become a transformative approach in areas such as smart windows, adaptive camouflage, radiative cooling, anticounterfeiting, and photovoltaics. Typical strategies primarily rely on tuning the intrinsic properties of electrochromic, thermochromic, or photochromic materials. Yet, these material-driven approaches still suffer from limited color purity, narrow tunability, slow response, and poor multifunction integration. An emerging alternative is to treat structural order as an independent physical design dimension. By organizing nanoscale building blocks into periodic, hierarchical, or reconfigurable architectures, one can manipulate light through Bragg diffraction, Mie scattering, plasmonic resonance, and graded-index effects. These mechanisms are difficult to access by chemical composition alone. Nature provides a rich library of such ordered designs. Photonic crystals, multilayers, porous networks, and graded-index arrays in organisms achieve efficient reflection, absorption, and transmission under ambient conditions. These biological systems show that precise control over orientation, periodicity, layer spacing, and refractive-index contrast can produce optical functions far beyond those of homogeneous materials. However, the inherent conflict between optical performance and mechanical robustness remains a formidable challenge. Although elastomer‐based electrospun nonwovens serve as a potential solution, they typically necessitate high nano‐filler loading for sufficient reflectance, which inevitably weakens interfacial bonding, leading to performance degradation and even structural failure during cyclic deformation. title_zh: Multiscale Freestanding Vertically Aligned CNT Heat Sink Enabling Multimodal Heat Dissipation by Conduction, Convection, and Radiation
title_en: Multiscale Freestanding Vertically Aligned CNT Heat Sink Enabling Multimodal Heat Dissipation by Conduction, Convection, and Radiation
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: A vertically aligned carbon nanotube (VACNT)-based heat sink is demonstrated for passive multimodal thermal management applicable for electronic and semiconductor devices. The VACNT enables multimodal heat dissipation through axial conduction, convection facilitated by its nanoporous morphology, and radiation enabled by its superior emissivity. While conventional metallic heat sinks suffer from low surface emissivity and require complex post-processing to enhance radiative cooling, the proposed VACNT overcomes these limitations by providing an inherent multiscale structural hierarchy without secondary surface treatments. The thermal conductivity of the freestanding VACNT (500 to 1500 µm heights) is characterized using laser flash analysis and differential scanning calorimetry as 32 to 40 W/mK. Evaluated on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W platform, the 1500 µm-high VACNT heat sink decreases the peak CPU temperature by 10.7°C compared with a bare CPU. The VACNT can be patterned into the topographic architecture to further improve heat dissipation by increasing the surface area, achieving a 6.7°C lower peak CPU temperature than a conventional aluminum heat sink. Cyclic stability test confirms consistent thermal performance over repeated use. The VACNT practically allows various configurational engineering by molding, rolling, scissoring, and tiling, showcasing its versatility for diverse thermal management applications.

title_zh: A Bioinspired Photon‐Gated Phase‐Change Textile for Two‐Stage Heat‐Flux Regulation of Building Envelopes
title_en: A Bioinspired Photon‐Gated Phase‐Change Textile for Two‐Stage Heat‐Flux Regulation of Building Envelopes
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: ABSTRACT Passive cooling textiles for buildings must do more than reflect sunlight; they must also buffer transient heat under real outdoor conditions. Here we report a continuous coaxial wet‐spinning strategy for fabricating a microencapsulated phase‐change material (mPCM)‐integrated radiative‐cooling meta‐fabric (MFRP), consisting of a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU)/hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN)/barium sulfate (BaSO 4 ) photon‐regulating sheath and a TPU/mPCM latent‐heat core. The spatially separated architecture integrates broadband solar reflection, atmospheric‐window emission, and phase‐change thermal buffering within one fiber platform. The optimized meta‐fabric shows high solar reflectance (95.44%), strong atmospheric‐window emissivity (96.21%), and a melting enthalpy of 102.28 J/g. In a representative sunny‐day test, MFRP reduced the chamber temperature by up to 10.36°C relative to the blank control; three‐day cement‐panel measurements further yielded an average peak‐temperature reduction of 7.51°C ± 2.17°C relative to bare cement. Energy‐balance analysis and climate‐scale modelling further indicate promising cooling‐energy and carbon‐reduction potential in hot and cooling‐dominated regions. These results establish wet‐spun radiative cooling/phase‐change material meta‐fabrics as continuously processable exterior textile candidates for passive building thermal management.

title_zh: Responses of surface radiative balance to wildfires differ across ecosystems
title_en: Responses of surface radiative balance to wildfires differ across ecosystems
abstract_zh: （网络收录文献，暂未整理中文简介；英文原文摘要见下方。）
abstract_en: Wildfires alter land surface albedo and temperature, modulating the radiative budget and climate. Previous studies have predominantly reported enhanced shortwave absorption induced by post-fire surface darkening over forests. Here, using two-decade (2001–2020) satellite observations of wildfires, we show that post-fire summer surface albedo and radiative balance shifts vary significantly across ecosystems. Broadleaf forests and grasslands exhibit a brightening effect, because the exposure of bright soils and rapid vegetation regrowth outweigh the deposition of dark carbonaceous residues. The post-fire surface brightening then amplifies the warming-driven radiative cooling. Conversely, in needleleaf forests, shrublands, and savannas, post-fire surface darkening increases shortwave absorption, yet warming-driven longwave radiative losses remain dominant, leading to net radiative cooling. Surface radiative fluxes exhibit high sensitivity to fire size in mid-to-high latitude regions driven by distinct fire-ecosystem feedbacks. Therefore, the ecosystem heterogeneity must be considered when assessing the effects of wildfires on the surface radiative budget and climate.
